clue.text: Educated people at home recount that single men get first-class return

parts.note: at home means in
to recount a story is to tell it
single is one, the Roman numeral I
gents are men, as on a lavatory door

indicators.note: return asks for the first-class rating to be read backwards, so the letter goes before the figure

parts.note: A1 means first-class, top-rated, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A snobbish account of learned folk at home and bachelors coming back first class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns A1 into 1A, read as IA; 'that' and 'get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a class of intellectuals, the cultured and learned section of society.

clue.text: Royal navy, for example

parts.note: royal and navy are read not as the fleet but as two named shades of one colour, each an example of it

explanation.surface: An example of a national fleet, the senior service.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Royal Navy; the trick is that royal and navy are both shades of the same colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal and navy are two well-known shades of this colour, so each is an example of it.

clue.text: Cases of free taramasalata and cheese

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so take the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: Free outer pots of taramasalata alongside some cheese on a Greek platter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases of' takes the first and last letters of 'free' (FE) and 'taramasalata' (TA).
explanation.definitionFit: It is a white brined Greek cheese made from sheep or goat milk.

clue.text: Sort of loaf around quietly — and get married

indicators.note: around means the loaf word goes round the quiet letter

parts.note: a sliced loaf is a sort of bread loaf
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop lounging about quietly and settle down to wedlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like a verb (idle), but 'Sort of loaf' is SLICED; 'and get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spliced is informal British slang for having wed, from joining two ropes together.

clue.text: Alters menu and starts to get excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of menu and starts are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef changes the menu as the diners begin to grow animated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' looks like an indicator for first letters, but it is anagram fodder along with 'menu'; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute something is to change its form or nature, so it is a synonym of alters.

clue.text: Multi-talented player, single chap, noisily excluded

parts.note: single means one
a chap is a man

indicators.note: noisily means as heard, so the word for excluded is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: excluded means barred or banned

explanation.surface: A versatile musician, a lone bloke who was thrown out for making a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisily' looks like part of the surface story of a loud player, but it signals the sound-alike: BANNED is heard as BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A street performer playing several instruments at once is the classic multi-talented musician of this kind.

clue.text: Plundered mains supply means hope is not lost

indicators.note: supply is read as supple-ly, in a pliant way, so the letters of plundered mains are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Even with the water mains looted, the supply holds and optimism survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun about the mains but is the adverb from supple, the anagram signal; 'means' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means never despair, an exhortation that there is still reason for optimism.

clue.text: Below California, for example, people have time — in a manner of speaking

parts.note: below means under
California is an example of a US state
people can mean men

explanation.surface: South of California, folk take their time, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people have time' joins MEN and T, with 'have' as a link; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying less than the truth, a deliberate playing-down, is a recognised figure of speech.

clue.text: The downgrading of envoys by soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the crossword abbreviation for soldiers
a legation is a body of diplomatic envoys

explanation.surface: Diplomats demoted at the hands of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; 'The', 'of' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and generally, being sent down to a lower division or rank is demotion.

clue.text: Petrol can be an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A fuel that could also knock you out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is a link; the fuel sense is American English, where British says petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage it is motor fuel; it also names nitrous oxide, the dentist's anaesthetic.

clue.text: Doctor of French has style

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French physician with real flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a fashion or manner, the way something is done.

clue.text: Stop, disheartened, seeing western Australian resort

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so the inner letters of stop go
western means the westernmost, leftmost letter of the word in an across entry

explanation.surface: A traveller halts, dispirited, at a holiday town in Western Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes TO from STOP to leave SP; 'western' picks A; 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa town is a health resort built round mineral springs.

clue.text: Line of least resistance past milers, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise, flagging a reshuffle of past milers

explanation.surface: Runners in a mile race slipping past, taking the easiest path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milers' looks like the subject of a racing picture, but 'past milers' is the fodder for the anagram signalled by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The low-pressure wake behind a moving runner or car offers the easiest ride to whoever follows.

clue.text: The attributes of decent links

parts.note: decent means proper, respectable
ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: The qualities of a respectable golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' suggests a golf course but means TIES; 'The' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristics or qualities of a thing are its properties in the scientific sense.

clue.text: Inclinations to cede tennis match

indicators.note: match is read as arrange or fit together, so the letters of cede tennis are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A player's urges to concede the tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like the tennis contest but signals the anagram; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendencies are leanings or propensities, the directions one is inclined to go.

clue.text: An acceptable standard — and not married!

parts.note: nor means and not
M is the abbreviation for married, as on forms

explanation.surface: Single life declared perfectly respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' sits as a link; NOR, the 'neither ... nor' word, stands for 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a usual pattern or benchmark that society regards as typical.

clue.text: A reason for being shipwrecked

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: Asking the cause of a ship being wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for being' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel run onto the shore or rocks and stuck there is stranded, the plight of a wreck.

clue.text: Way of approaching the last dance

indicators.note: dance means the letters of the last caper about into a new order

explanation.surface: Moving towards someone during the final dance of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance' looks like a noun (the last dance) but is a verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is moving quietly and secretly, the manner in which a hunter creeps up on prey.

clue.text: Noise that might point to the critical moment?

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
the crunch is the decisive moment, when it comes to the crunch

explanation.surface: A sound that may signal that the decisive moment has come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that might' and 'to' are links; 'point' is a compass point, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunching or crumpling sound, such as feet on gravel, is this sort of noise.

clue.text: Former pimp gets executed

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the word for pimp loses its first letter

parts.note: ponce is British slang for a pimp

explanation.surface: A one-time procurer is put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link; PONCE is a British slang word for a pimp, and beheading it leaves the word for former.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past, as in a once-great city.

clue.text: Tax burden following strike

indicators.note: following means the burden word comes after the strike word

parts.note: to strike out is to excise, cut away
a duty is a burden or obligation

explanation.surface: A heavy levy imposed after industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but means cut out (EXCISE); 'following' puts DUTY after it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a government levy on goods such as alcohol and tobacco, a kind of tax.

clue.text: Show of hesitation accepting a prize for bullfighting

indicators.note: accepting means the hesitation sound takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Hesitating before taking a trophy for fighting bulls.
explanation.walkthrough: A successful matador may be awarded one of the dead bull's ears as a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish bullfighting a matador who performs well is given the bull's ear as an honour.

clue.text: Managed area within armed forces

indicators.note: within means the area letter sits inside the forces abbreviation

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for one of the armed forces; the letters running backwards across within armed are a coincidence, as no word signals a reversal

explanation.surface: A district run by the military.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's naval service.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to manage it, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Note way of attracting attention

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A whispered note as a way of catching someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the answer is the whispered hiss used for catching someone's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an interjection whispered for catching someone's notice discreetly.

clue.text: Do they prove a case for royal residences?

definitions.text: Do they prove a case for royal residences?

parts.words: Do they prove a case for royal residences
parts.note: read as the halls where lawsuits are tried, and also as chambers in a monarch's court

explanation.surface: Asking whether palaces need a legal argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Cases are tried in halls of justice, while a royal court has many chambers of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the halls where legal cases are heard, and literally chambers at a royal court.

clue.text: Large tents of the highest quality

explanation.surface: Big marquees of the finest kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Circus big tents are 'big tops', so the plural alone can stand for large tents.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus marquee is a big top; informally, the best of all is described as the very best.

clue.text: God is full of good intentions

indicators.note: full of means the letters sit inside the words good intentions

explanation.surface: The deity is overflowing with benevolence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor.

clue.text: Objects to placing cake next to pies

indicators.note: placing means arranging, so the letters of cake next to pies are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests about a cake sitting beside the pies on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a noun but is the verb; the whole of 'cake next to pies' is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage at something is to protest or object to it.
